stem: "चंद्रमा" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: शशि (also राकेश, इंदु, सोम) means the moon. भानु, रवि and दिवाकर are all names of the sun.

stem: "पृथ्वी" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: वसुधा (also धरती, भूमि, वसुंधरा) means the earth. अंबर, व्योम and नभ all mean the sky.

stem: "उदय" का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
explanation: उदय (rising) is the opposite of अस्त (setting), as in सूर्योदय and सूर्यास्त. उत्थान and उदित are close in meaning to उदय.

stem: "सजीव" का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
explanation: सजीव (living) is opposite to निर्जीव (lifeless). सजग, सक्रिय and सचेत mean alert or active, not the opposite.

stem: "जो दूसरों का उपकार करता हो" के लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
explanation: परोपकारी is one who does good to others. उपकृत is the person who received the favour, and कृतज्ञ is one who is grateful for it.

stem: "जो दिखाई न दे" के लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
explanation: अदृश्य means invisible. दृष्टिहीन is a person who cannot see, and पारदर्शी is something you can see through.

stem: "हस्त" का तद्भव रूप क्या है?
explanation: हस्त is the tatsam (Sanskrit) word and हाथ its tadbhav form. कर and पाणि are tatsam synonyms of हस्त, and भुजा means the arm.

stem: "आस्तीन का साँप" मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
explanation: आस्तीन का साँप is a friend who turns out to be a traitor, like a snake hidden in one's own sleeve.

stem: "घी के दीये जलाना" मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
explanation: घी के दीये जलाना means to celebrate with great joy, as when long-awaited good news arrives.

stem: "नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा" लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है:
explanation: Someone who cannot dance blames the uneven courtyard: a person hides his own lack of skill by finding fault elsewhere.

stem: "गणेश" का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
explanation: गण + ईश: अ + ई = ए, which is गुण संधि (like परमेश्वर = परम + ईश्वर). गण + एश would give गणैश (वृद्धि) and गणि + ईश would give गणीश.

stem: "नीलकमल" में कौन-सा समास है?
explanation: नीलकमल = नीला है जो कमल. The first word describes the second (विशेषण-विशेष्य), so it is कर्मधारय समास.

stem: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द पुल्लिंग है?
explanation: पर्वत is masculine (ऊँचा पर्वत). नदी, पुस्तक and सड़क are feminine (बहती नदी, मोटी पुस्तक, चौड़ी सड़क).

stem: "कथा" का बहुवचन (मूल रूप, बिना विभक्ति) क्या है?
explanation: Feminine nouns ending in आ take एँ in the plural: कथा to कथाएँ. कथाओं is the oblique form used before a विभक्ति (कथाओं में).

stem: "पद्मावत" के रचनाकार कौन हैं?
explanation: पद्मावत was written by मलिक मुहम्मद जायसी, a Sufi poet of the प्रेममार्गी branch of the भक्ति period.

stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to AFFLUENT.
explanation: An affluent person or family has plenty of money: wealthy. Poor is the opposite.

stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to SERENE.
explanation: Serene means calm and peaceful, as in a serene lake. Noisy and angry are near opposites.

stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to RIGID.
explanation: Rigid means unable to bend; flexible means bending easily. Stiff and firm are close to rigid.

stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to ADVANCE.
explanation: To advance is to move forward; to retreat is to move back. Proceed and progress are synonyms.

stem: Fill in the blank: The man was charged ___ theft.
explanation: In the legal sense, a person is charged with an offence. Accused takes of (accused of theft).

stem: Fill in the blank: She is ___ university teacher.
explanation: University begins with a "yu" consonant sound, so it takes a, even though it is spelt with a vowel.

stem: Fill in the blank: By next March, she ___ her degree.
explanation: An action that will be finished before a point in the future takes the future perfect: will have + past participle.

stem: Choose the correctly spelt word.
explanation: Occasion has a double c and a single s: o-c-c-a-s-i-o-n.

stem: What does the idiom "to call it a day" mean?
options: To stop working for the day
explanation: To call it a day is to decide to stop working, usually because enough has been done.

stem: Choose one word for: one who knows everything.
explanation: Omniscient means all-knowing. Omnipotent is all-powerful and omnipresent is present everywhere.

stem: Choose the passive form of: The farmer ploughs the field.
options: The field has been ploughed by the farmer.
The field is ploughed by the farmer.
The field is being ploughed by the farmer.
The field was ploughed by the farmer.
explanation: Simple present active (ploughs) becomes is/are + past participle in the passive: is ploughed.

stem: Choose the indirect form of: He said to me, "I will help you."
options: He told me that he will help me.
He told me that he would help me.
He said me that he would help me.
He told me that I would help him.
explanation: Said to me becomes told me, will becomes would, and I/you become he/me. "Said me" is wrong: said takes to before its object.

stem:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.

The news are very encouraging today.
explanation: News is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb: The news is very encouraging.

stem: In the sentence "My cousin is junior than me by three years", choose the best replacement for "junior than me".
explanation: Senior, junior, superior and inferior take to, not than: My cousin is junior to me by three years.

stem: Fill in the blank: Unless you work hard, you ___ pass the exam.
explanation: Unless means if not and, like if in a real future condition, takes the simple present with will in the main clause.

stem: What is 35% of 840?
A cycle bought for ₹750 is sold for ₹840. What is the profit percent?
explanation: Profit = 840 - 750 = ₹90, and profit % = 90/750 × 100 = 12%. Dividing by the selling price (90/840) gives the wrong 10.7%.

stem: What is the simple interest on ₹5,600 at 7.5% per annum for 3 years?
explanation: SI = P × R × T / 100 = 5,600 × 7.5 × 3 / 100 = ₹1,260. ₹420 is the interest for one year only and ₹840 for two years.

stem: If A : B = 3 : 5 and B : C = 4 : 7, what is A : B : C?
explanation: Make B the same in both: A : B = 12 : 20 and B : C = 20 : 35, so A : B : C = 12 : 20 : 35.

stem: What is the average of 23, 27, 31, 35, 39 and 43?
explanation: Sum = 198 and there are 6 numbers, so the average is 198 ÷ 6 = 33. For evenly spaced numbers it is halfway between the first and last.

stem: A can finish a job in 21 days and B in 28 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
explanation: Together they do 1/21 + 1/28 = (4 + 3)/84 = 1/12 of the job a day, so they need 12 days. Averaging the days (24.5) or adding them (49) is a common slip.

stem: A train 180 m long runs at 54 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a pole?
explanation: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. To pass a pole the train covers its own length: 180 ÷ 15 = 12 seconds. 15 is the speed in m/s, not the time.

stem: What is the HCF of 105 and 175?
explanation: 105 = 3 × 5 × 7 and 175 = 5² × 7, so the HCF is 5 × 7 = 35. 525 is their LCM.

stem: What is the area of a circle of radius 10.5 cm? (Take π = 22/7.)
explanation: Area = πr² = 22/7 × 10.5 × 10.5 = 346.5 cm². 66 cm is the circumference, 2πr.

stem: What are the roots of x² - 9x + 20 = 0?
explanation: Find two numbers with product 20 and sum 9: 4 and 5. So (x - 4)(x - 5) = 0 and x = 4 or 5. 2 and 10 multiply to 20 but add to 12.

stem: What is the 10th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, 15, ...?
explanation: a = 3 and d = 4, so the 10th term = a + 9d = 3 + 36 = 39. Using 10d instead of 9d gives the wrong 43, and 47 is the 12th term.

stem: What is the value of cos² 60° + sin² 30°?
explanation: cos 60° = 1/2 and sin 30° = 1/2, so the value is 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2. It is not sin² + cos² of the same angle, so it is not 1.

stem: What is the median of 7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 1 and 13?
explanation: Put the numbers in order first: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. With 7 values the median is the 4th, which is 7.

stem: A bag has 5 red, 7 blue and 3 white balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is white?
explanation: There are 15 balls and 3 are white, so the probability is 3/15 = 1/5. 1/4 wrongly compares white (3) with the other balls (12).

stem: What is the volume of a cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 8 cm? (Take π = 22/7.)
explanation: Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 × 8 = 308 cm³. 176 is the curved surface area, 2πrh, in cm².

stem: Which law of 1919 allowed the government to detain people without trial and led Gandhi to call a nationwide hartal?
explanation: The Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed detention without trial. Protests against it led to the hartal of April 1919 and, in Amritsar, to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

stem: In the northern plains, khadar is:
explanation: Khadar is the newer, finer alluvium renewed by floods every year, very fertile. Bhangar is the older alluvium, higher up and often with kankar nodules.

stem: After Gandhi's arrest in 1930, who led the salt satyagraha raid on the Dharasana salt works?
explanation: Sarojini Naidu, with Imam Sahib, led the non-violent volunteers at Dharasana in May 1930, where they were beaten but did not hit back.

stem: Zaid crops such as watermelon and cucumber are grown:
explanation: Zaid is the short summer season between the rabi and kharif seasons, used for watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber and fodder.

stem: The Dandi March of 1930 was undertaken to break which law?
explanation: Gandhi walked from Sabarmati to Dandi and made salt from sea water, breaking the salt law and starting the Civil Disobedience Movement.

stem: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
explanation: It crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

stem: At which session of 1907 did the Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists?
explanation: At the Surat session of 1907 the Moderates, led by Gokhale, and the Extremists, led by Tilak, split. They came together again at Lucknow in 1916.

stem: In which hemispheres does the Indian mainland lie?
explanation: The mainland lies between about 8°N and 37°N and 68°E and 97°E, so it is entirely in the northern and eastern hemispheres.

stem: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Gandhi and:
explanation: The Poona Pact gave the depressed classes reserved seats in the legislatures, elected by the general electorate, in place of separate electorates.

stem: Koderma in Jharkhand is known for which mineral?
explanation: The Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt is a leading mica area. Mica is used in electrical and electronic goods.

stem: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of which prison?
explanation: On 14 July 1789 a crowd stormed the Bastille, a fortress-prison in Paris that stood for the king's power.

stem: The Krishna river rises near:
explanation: The Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats. The Godavari rises near Nashik, the Narmada at Amarkantak and the Kaveri at Talakaveri.

stem: Who was the chief architect of German unification, completed in 1871?
explanation: Bismarck, the chief minister of Prussia, unified Germany through wars, and in 1871 the Prussian king was proclaimed German Emperor. Mazzini, Garibaldi and Cavour worked for Italian unification.

stem: The Son river, which joins the Ganga near Patna, rises at:
explanation: The Son rises on the Amarkantak plateau, near the source of the Narmada, and flows north-east to join the Ganga upstream of Patna.

stem: Which Magadha king built the fort of Pataligrama, which later grew into Pataliputra?
explanation: Ajatashatru of the Haryanka dynasty fortified the village of Pataligrama on the Ganga. His successors made Pataliputra the capital of Magadha.

stem: Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka that help mangoes ripen are called:
explanation: Mango showers fall before the monsoon. Kalbaisakhi are evening storms in Bengal, and loo is the hot dry summer wind of the northern plains.

stem: Which Chinese pilgrim visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II?
explanation: Fa-Hien came in the early 5th century under Chandragupta II. Hiuen Tsang came under Harsha, and Megasthenes was a Greek envoy at the Mauryan court.

stem: Which best describes the organised sector?
options: Registered, with regular terms of work
explanation: Organised-sector enterprises are registered with the government and follow its rules on pay, hours and leave. Private firms can be organised too.

stem: The 29 subjects given to panchayats are listed in which Schedule of the Constitution?
explanation: The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects for panchayats; the 74th added the Twelfth Schedule with 18 for municipalities.

stem: MGNREGA 2005 guarantees how many days of wage employment a year to a rural household?
explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act promises 100 days of work a year to every rural household that asks for it.

stem: Under the 73rd Amendment, at least what share of seats in panchayats must be reserved for women?
explanation: The Constitution sets a minimum of one-third. States may give more: Bihar reserves half the seats in its panchayats for women.

stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:
explanation: The United Nations Development Programme publishes the HDI in its Human Development Report, combining health, education and income.

stem: Under which Article can a High Court issue writs to enforce rights?
explanation: Article 226 lets High Courts issue writs for fundamental rights and other legal rights; Article 32 is the Supreme Court's power. Article 214 just says each state shall have a High Court.

stem: Which body certifies industrial and consumer goods with the ISI mark?
explanation: The ISI mark is given by the Bureau of Indian Standards. AGMARK is used for farm products.

stem: Who presides over the Lok Sabha when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent?
options: A member from the panel of chairpersons
explanation: The Speaker names a panel of chairpersons, and one of them presides when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are away.

stem: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are joined in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
explanation: In parallel, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6, so R = 2 Ω. The combined resistance is less than the smaller resistor; 9 Ω is the series total.

stem: What is the power of a concave lens of focal length 25 cm?
explanation: Power = 1/f with f in metres. f = -0.25 m for a concave lens, so P = -4 dioptres. Using 0.25 without inverting gives the wrong 0.25 D.

stem: A ray falls on a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the normal. 55° would be measured from the mirror.

stem: A current of 0.5 A flows through a resistor of 20 Ω. What is the potential difference across it?
explanation: Ohm's law: V = IR = 0.5 × 20 = 10 V. Dividing 20 by 0.5 gives the wrong 40 V.

stem: Two resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
explanation: In parallel, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3, so R = 3 Ω. In series they would add to 12 Ω.

stem: A solution turns blue litmus red. Its pH is most likely:
explanation: Turning blue litmus red shows an acid, and acids have a pH below 7. Bases turn red litmus blue and have a pH above 7.

stem: What is the common name of calcium oxychloride (CaOCl₂)?
explanation: Calcium oxychloride is bleaching powder, made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime. It is used to disinfect drinking water.

stem: Iron rusts when it is exposed to:
options: Boiled water in a sealed tube
explanation: Rusting needs both oxygen and water. Dry air or boiled water with no dissolved air will not rust iron.

stem: Quicklime reacts with water to form slaked lime. What type of reaction is this?
explanation: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂: two substances combine into one, and heat is given out.

stem: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing:
explanation: The modern periodic law says properties repeat with atomic number. Mendeleev had arranged elements by atomic mass.

stem: Which plant tissue carries the food made in the leaves to other parts of the plant?
explanation: Phloem carries sugars from the leaves to the roots, stems and fruits. Xylem carries water and minerals up from the roots.

stem: How many chambers does the heart of a fish have?
explanation: A fish heart has one atrium and one ventricle and pumps blood through the gills once per circuit. Amphibians have three chambers, and birds and mammals four.

stem: In humans, urine is stored in the:
explanation: The kidneys make urine, the ureters carry it to the urinary bladder where it is stored, and the urethra lets it out.

stem: In Mendel's monohybrid cross, what is the phenotypic ratio of tall to short plants in the F2 generation?
explanation: Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: three tall to one short. 1 : 2 : 1 is the genotypic ratio and 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 is from a dihybrid cross.

stem: Which of these wastes is biodegradable?
explanation: Bacteria and fungi can break down vegetable peels. Plastic, glass and aluminium stay in the environment for a very long time.

stem: Bihar Diwas, marking the creation of Bihar as a separate province in 1912, is celebrated on:
explanation: Bihar was separated from the Bengal Presidency on 22 March 1912. (1 April 1936 is when Odisha was separated from Bihar.)

stem: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas), on Sardar Patel's birth anniversary, is observed on:
explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born on 31 October 1875; the day has been observed as National Unity Day since 2014.

stem: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar as a new state in:
explanation: Jharkhand became a separate state on 15 November 2000, taking the Chota Nagpur plateau and its mineral belt.

stem: The International Court of Justice sits at:
explanation: The International Court of Justice, the UN's main court, sits in the Peace Palace at The Hague, in the Netherlands.

stem: The Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is at:
explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple marks where the Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2002.

stem: How many players make up a polo team on the field?
explanation: A polo team has four mounted players on the field.

stem: Madhubani painting comes from which region of Bihar?
explanation: Madhubani or Mithila painting, done with natural colours and fine line work, grew in the Mithila region of north Bihar.

stem: In which language did Rabindranath Tagore first write Gitanjali, the work behind his 1913 Nobel Prize?
explanation: Gitanjali was written in Bengali; Tagore's own English version won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

stem: Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar's only tiger reserve, is in which district?
explanation: Valmiki National Park and Tiger Reserve lies in West Champaran, on the Nepal border, next to Nepal's Chitwan National Park.

stem: The Jnanpith Award is given for excellence in:
explanation: The Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honour, is given to writers for their contribution to Indian literature.

stem: Which animal is the state animal of Bihar?
explanation: The gaur, or Indian bison, is Bihar's state animal. The house sparrow is the state bird.

stem: The Gateway of India is in which city?
explanation: The Gateway of India stands on the waterfront of Mumbai; India Gate is in New Delhi.

stem: Dr Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, was born at Ziradei in which district of Bihar?
explanation: Rajendra Prasad was born at Ziradei in present-day Siwan district in 1884.

stem: Which river was declared the National River of India in 2008?
explanation: The Ganga was declared India's National River in November 2008. It flows west to east across Bihar, past Buxar, Patna and Bhagalpur.

stem: Which leader of the 1857 revolt in Bihar came from Jagdishpur?
explanation: Babu Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur (Bhojpur district) led the revolt in Bihar at about 80 years of age.

stem: "आकाश" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: गगन (also अंबर, नभ, व्योम) means the sky. धरणी is earth, सलिल is water and अनिल is wind.

stem: "घोड़ा" का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
explanation: अश्व (also तुरंग, हय, घोटक) means horse. गर्दभ is a donkey, उष्ट्र a camel and शृगाल a jackal.

stem: "आशा" का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
explanation: आशा (hope) is opposite to निराशा (despair). अभिलाषा (wish) and आस्था (faith) are not opposites.

stem: "प्राचीन" का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
explanation: प्राचीन (ancient) is opposite to अर्वाचीन (modern). पुरातन is a synonym, प्राच्य means eastern and प्रवीण means skilled.

stem: "जो बहुत कम भोजन करता हो" के लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
explanation: अल्पाहारी is one who eats little (अल्प = little). शाकाहारी, मांसाहारी and सर्वाहारी describe what is eaten, not how much.

stem: "जिसकी गिनती न की जा सके" के लिए एक शब्द क्या है?
explanation: अगणित (also अनगिनत) means countless. अनुपम and अतुलनीय mean matchless, and अजेय means unconquerable.

stem: "कर्म" का तद्भव रूप क्या है?
explanation: कर्म (tatsam) becomes काम in everyday Hindi. कार्य, कृत्य and क्रिया are themselves tatsam words.

stem: "अँगूठा दिखाना" मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
explanation: अँगूठा दिखाना means to refuse flatly, usually at the moment help was expected.

stem: "कान भरना" मुहावरे का अर्थ है:
explanation: कान भरना means to poison someone's mind against another by telling tales (चुगली).

stem: "का बरखा जब कृषि सुखानी" लोकोक्ति का अर्थ है:
explanation: What use is rain once the crop has dried? Help that comes too late is useless. The line is from तुलसीदास.

stem: "महेश" का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
explanation: महा + ईश: आ + ई = ए, which is गुण संधि. महा + एश would give महैश (वृद्धि) and महि + ईश would give महीश.

stem: "चौराहा" में कौन-सा समास है?
explanation: चौराहा = चार राहों का समूह. When the first part is a number and the whole names a group, it is द्विगु समास.

stem: "मोहन ने गरीबों को कपड़े दिए।" इस वाक्य में "गरीबों को" में कौन-सा कारक है?
explanation: When को marks the person for whom something is given, it is संप्रदान कारक. The thing given (कपड़े) is the कर्म.

stem: "प्रतिदिन" शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
explanation: प्रति + दिन = प्रतिदिन (every day). दिन is the root word, not the prefix.

stem: "रश्मिरथी" के रचनाकार कौन हैं?
explanation: रश्मिरथी, a long poem on Karna, is by रामधारी सिंह दिनकर, the राष्ट्रकवि born in Simaria, Begusarai district of Bihar.

stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to VICTORY.
explanation: Victory and triumph both mean a win. Defeat is the opposite.

stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to PROSPER.
explanation: To prosper is to do well and grow successful: to flourish. Decline is the opposite.

stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to HAUGHTY.
explanation: A haughty person behaves as if better than others; a modest person does not boast. Proud is close in meaning to haughty.

stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to SCARCITY.
explanation: Scarcity is a shortage of something; abundance is a plentiful supply. Shortage and famine mean much the same as scarcity.

stem: Fill in the blank: He prides himself ___ his honesty.
explanation: The verb pride oneself takes on: He prides himself on his honesty. (The adjective proud takes of.)

stem: Fill in the blank: Each of the students ___ a prize.
explanation: Each is singular, so it takes a singular verb (has won), even when followed by "of the students".

stem: Which of these words is spelt correctly?
explanation: Accommodate has a double c and a double m: a-c-c-o-m-m-o-d-a-t-e.

stem: What does the idiom "to bite off more than you can chew" mean?
options: To take on more than you can manage
explanation: To bite off more than you can chew is to accept a task that is too big or difficult for you to finish.

stem: Choose one word for: a place where birds are kept.
explanation: An aviary houses birds. An apiary keeps bees, an aquarium fish and a kennel dogs.

stem: Choose the passive form of: Who wrote this letter?
options: By whom was this letter written?
By whom this letter is written?
Whom was this letter wrote by?
explanation: Who becomes by whom, and the simple past wrote becomes was written, keeping the question order: By whom was this letter written?

stem: Choose the indirect form of: He said to her, "Are you coming to the meeting?"
options: He asked her that was she coming to the meeting.
He said to her if she is coming to the meeting.
He asked her was she coming to the meeting?
He asked her if she was coming to the meeting.
explanation: A yes-no question is reported with asked + if or whether, in statement word order, with the tense moved back: are coming becomes was coming.

stem:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.

He is one of the best player that our school has produced.
options: He is one of the best
explanation: One of the best is followed by a plural noun: one of the best players.

stem:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.

The children were playing in the garden.
explanation: The plural subject children takes were, and the sentence is correct as it stands.

stem: In the sentence "She is capable to do the work", choose the best replacement for "capable to do".
explanation: Capable is followed by of + -ing form: She is capable of doing the work.

stem: Fill in the blank: I wish I ___ a bird.
explanation: An unreal wish about the present uses were for every person: I wish I were a bird.

stem: A number is increased by 30% and the result is then decreased by 30%. What is the net change?
explanation: 100 becomes 130, and 30% off 130 is 91, so the net change is a 9% decrease. In general a rise and fall of x% gives a fall of x²/100 %.

stem: An article marked at ₹1,500 is sold after two successive discounts of 10% and 20%. What is the selling price?
explanation: 1,500 × 0.9 = 1,350, then 1,350 × 0.8 = ₹1,080. A single 30% discount (₹1,050) is not the same as 10% then 20%.

stem: What is the compound interest on ₹12,500 at 8% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
explanation: Amount = 12,500 × 1.08 × 1.08 = ₹14,580, so CI = ₹2,080. Simple interest would be only ₹2,000.

stem: A father is 4 times as old as his son. After 5 years he will be 3 times as old as his son. What is the son's present age?
explanation: Let the son be s. Then 4s + 5 = 3(s + 5), so s = 10. The father is 40; in 5 years 45 = 3 × 15. 15 is the son's age in 5 years, and 40 the father's age now.

stem: A invests ₹6,000 for 12 months and B invests ₹8,000 for 6 months. Out of a profit of ₹5,000, what is A's share?
explanation: Shares go by money × time: 6,000 × 12 = 72,000 and 8,000 × 6 = 48,000, a ratio of 3 : 2. A gets 3/5 of 5,000 = ₹3,000.

stem: A bus goes from one town to another at 45 km/h and comes back by the same road at 36 km/h. What is its average speed for the round trip?
explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2ab/(a + b) = 2 × 45 × 36 / 81 = 40 km/h, not the simple average of 40.5.

stem: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 10 and 15 hours, and pipe C empties it in 30 hours. With all three open, in how many hours will the empty tank fill?
explanation: Net rate = 1/10 + 1/15 - 1/30 = (3 + 2 - 1)/30 = 4/30 of the tank an hour, so it fills in 30/4 = 7.5 hours. Ignoring C gives 6 hours.

stem: What is the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 12, 15 or 20?
explanation: LCM of 12, 15 and 20 is 60, so the number is 60 + 4 = 64.

stem: What is the length of the diagonal of a rectangle 48 m long and 14 m wide?
explanation: Diagonal = √(48² + 14²) = √(2304 + 196) = √2500 = 50 m. Adding the sides (62 m) ignores Pythagoras.

stem: If x + y = 14 and x - y = 4, what is the value of x?
explanation: Adding the two equations gives 2x = 18, so x = 9 and y = 5. 7 is half of 14, which ignores the second equation.

stem: What is the sum of the first 15 terms of the AP 2, 5, 8, 11, ...?
If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is an acute angle, what is cos θ?
explanation: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, so cos² θ = 1 - 9/25 = 16/25 and cos θ = 4/5 (a 3-4-5 triangle). 3/4 is tan θ.

stem: What is the total surface area of a cube with an edge of 6 cm?
explanation: A cube has 6 square faces: 6 × 6² = 216 cm². 144 cm² is only the 4 side faces.

stem: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
explanation: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5: three of six outcomes, so 1/2. 1 is not a prime number.

stem: What is 25% of 480 + 40% of 150?
explanation: 25% of 480 = 120 and 40% of 150 = 60, so the total is 180.

stem: At which session in 1907 did the Congress split between the Moderates and the Extremists?
explanation: The Congress split at Surat in 1907. The two groups came together again at Lucknow in 1916.

stem: Which soil, formed on crystalline igneous rocks, looks red because of iron?
explanation: Red soil develops on old crystalline rocks where rainfall is low; iron spread through it gives the red colour, and it looks yellow when hydrated.

stem: Who coined the slogan "Inquilab Zindabad"?
explanation: The poet and freedom fighter Maulana Hasrat Mohani coined Inquilab Zindabad in 1921. Bhagat Singh and his comrades later made it famous.

stem: Makhana (fox nut), a speciality of north Bihar, grows in:
explanation: Makhana is the seed of a water plant grown in ponds and wetlands, mainly in the Mithila region of Bihar.

stem: The Swadeshi Movement of 1905 began as a protest against:
explanation: When Bengal was divided in 1905, nationalists called for boycotting British goods and using Indian-made (swadeshi) goods.

stem: Pulicat Lake, a coastal lagoon, lies on the border of Andhra Pradesh and:
explanation: Pulicat Lake straddles the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border; the island of Sriharikota separates it from the Bay of Bengal.

stem: Which of these Harappan sites is in present-day Haryana?
explanation: Rakhigarhi, in Hisar district, is one of the largest Harappan sites. Lothal and Dholavira are in Gujarat and Kalibangan is in Rajasthan.

stem: Bauxite is the ore of which metal?
explanation: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite. Odisha has India's largest bauxite reserves.

stem: The Bhakti saint Kabir is traditionally said to be a disciple of:
explanation: Tradition makes Kabir a disciple of Ramananda in Varanasi. Tulsidas and Chaitanya lived later, and Namdev lived earlier, in Maharashtra.

stem: Which channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives?
explanation: The Eight Degree Channel lies between Minicoy in Lakshadweep and the Maldives. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

stem: Which leader wrote Gita Rahasya while imprisoned at Mandalay?
explanation: Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya during his imprisonment at Mandalay in Burma (1908 to 1914).

stem: Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?
explanation: Anamudi in Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats. Doddabetta is in the Nilgiris, Mahendragiri in the Eastern Ghats and Guru Shikhar in the Aravallis.

stem: Who led the volunteer army known as the Red Shirts in the unification of Italy?
explanation: Garibaldi's Red Shirts took Sicily and Naples in 1860. Mazzini founded Young Italy, and Cavour led as Sardinia-Piedmont's chief minister.

stem: The North-South Corridor of the national highways links Srinagar with:
explanation: The North-South Corridor runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari; the East-West Corridor runs from Silchar to Porbandar.

stem: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
explanation: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, now Republic Day.

stem: Per capita income is the national income divided by the:
explanation: Per capita income is average income: total national income divided by the whole population.

stem: What is the status of the right to property today?
explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed property from the Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

stem: Which institution supervises the working of banks in India?
explanation: The RBI watches over banks, for example the cash they must hold. The State Bank of India is a commercial bank itself.

stem: A no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers can be moved only in:
explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3), so a no-confidence motion can be moved only there.

stem: Which organisation aims to liberalise international trade?
explanation: The WTO, set up in 1995, makes rules for trade between countries and aims to remove trade barriers.

stem: The first hour of a sitting of Parliament, when members ask ministers questions, is called:
explanation: A sitting usually opens with Question Hour, when members question ministers about the work of their ministries.

stem: When more people work on a farm than are needed, so that removing some does not lower output, it is called:
explanation: Disguised (hidden) unemployment is common in agriculture: family members all appear to work, but their work adds nothing extra.

stem: In which list of the Seventh Schedule is education placed?
explanation: Education was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment (1976), so both the Union and the states can make laws on it.

stem: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
explanation: Coal took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced once used. Sun, wind and forests can be renewed.

stem: The Chief Minister of a state is appointed by the:
explanation: Under Article 164 the Governor appoints the Chief Minister, usually the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly.

stem: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 30 cm. What is its focal length?
explanation: For a spherical mirror f = R/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm.

stem: For a young adult with normal vision, the near point of the eye is at about:
explanation: The least distance of distinct vision is about 25 cm; nearer than that, the eye lens cannot curve enough to focus.

stem: The twinkling of stars is due to:
explanation: Starlight is bent by air layers of changing density, so the apparent position and brightness of the star keep changing. Planets are closer and look like discs, so they do not twinkle.

stem: An electric heater draws 5 A at 220 V. What is its power?
explanation: P = VI = 220 × 5 = 1100 W. 44 is the resistance in ohms (220 ÷ 5), not the power.

stem: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest pointing in which direction?
explanation: The Earth's magnetic field turns a freely suspended magnet until its north pole points roughly to geographic north, so it lies north-south.

stem: An acid reacts with a base to form:
explanation: Neutralisation gives a salt and water, for example HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Hydrogen is given off when an acid reacts with a metal.

stem: Which allotrope of carbon is a good conductor of electricity?
explanation: In graphite each carbon is bonded to three others, leaving electrons free to move, so it conducts. Diamond, with four bonds per atom, does not.

stem: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
explanation: Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series and reacts violently with water. Gold is among the least reactive.

stem: Which is the first member of the alkane series?
explanation: Methane, CH₄, has one carbon atom. Ethene and ethyne have double and triple bonds, so they are not alkanes.

stem: Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of:
explanation: Soap is made by heating fats or oils with an alkali (saponification), which gives sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids.

stem: Digestion of starch begins in the:
explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth begins breaking starch into sugar. The stomach starts the digestion of proteins.

stem: Exchange of gases in a leaf takes place mainly through the:
explanation: Stomata are tiny pores on the leaf surface that let in carbon dioxide and let out oxygen and water vapour.

stem: Which plant hormone makes a shoot bend towards light?
explanation: Auxin collects on the shaded side of the shoot, which grows faster, so the shoot bends towards the light.

stem: Iodine is needed by which gland to make the hormone thyroxine?
explanation: The thyroid uses iodine to make thyroxine; too little iodine causes goitre, which is why salt is iodised.

stem: Under the 10 per cent law, how much of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next?
explanation: Only about 10% of the energy is passed on; the rest is used in life processes or lost as heat, which is why food chains are short.

stem: The Vikramshila Mahavihara near Bhagalpur was founded by which Pala king?
explanation: Dharmapala founded Vikramshila around 800 CE. Gopala was the first Pala king.

stem: Which country hosted the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930?
explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930.

stem: The Sonepur cattle fair is held where the Ganga meets which river?
explanation: The Sonepur Mela, one of Asia's oldest cattle fairs, begins at Kartik Purnima at the meeting of the Gandak and the Ganga.

stem: The Ajanta caves are in which state?
explanation: The Ajanta caves, with Buddhist paintings, are in Aurangabad district of Maharashtra.

stem: The tomb of Sher Shah Suri is at:
explanation: Sher Shah's tomb stands in the middle of a lake at Sasaram, in Rohtas district.

stem: Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
explanation: Japan's own name, Nippon, means the origin of the sun.

stem: Takht Sri Harimandir Ji, Patna Sahib, marks the birthplace of:
explanation: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, was born in Patna in 1666. Patna Sahib is one of the five Takhts.

stem: Every Nobel Prize is presented in Sweden except the Peace Prize, which is presented in:
explanation: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway; the other prizes are presented in Stockholm.

stem: The Second Buddhist Council was held at:
explanation: The First Council was at Rajgir, the Second at Vaishali and the Third at Pataliputra under Ashoka.

stem: The term "duck" is used in which sport?
explanation: In cricket a batter who is out without scoring is out for a duck.

stem: At which place in Bihar did Mahavira attain nirvana?
explanation: Mahavira died at Pawapuri in Nalanda district, where the Jal Mandir stands. He was born at Kundagram near Vaishali.

stem: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
explanation: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Paris hosted the second Games in 1900.

stem: Bhagalpur is famous for which kind of silk?
explanation: Bhagalpur, the Silk City, is known for tussar silk. Muga and eri silk come mainly from Assam.

stem: Chhath Puja, a major festival of Bihar, is dedicated to:
explanation: Chhath Puja honours Surya, the Sun god, with prayers at rivers and ponds at sunset and sunrise.

stem: The Barabar caves, among the oldest rock-cut caves in India, belong to which period?
explanation: The Barabar caves in Jehanabad district were cut in the 3rd century BCE under the Mauryas and given to the Ajivika sect.

stem: "पीपर पात सरिस मन डोला" में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
explanation: The mind is compared with a peepal leaf using the comparing word सरिस (like), so it is उपमा. रूपक makes the two the same, with no comparing word.

stem: किस शब्द की वर्तनी सही है?
explanation: अति + अधिक = अत्यधिक (यण संधि). अत्याधिक is a very common misspelling.

stem: "लिखावट" शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय है?
explanation: लिख + आवट = लिखावट. The same suffix gives सजावट and बनावट.

stem: हास्य रस का स्थायी भाव क्या है?
explanation: हास्य रस has हास as its स्थायी भाव. रति belongs to शृंगार, शोक to करुण and क्रोध to रौद्र.

stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ADEQUATE.
explanation: Adequate means enough for what is needed, that is, sufficient. Scarce is the opposite.

stem: Choose the word opposite in meaning to OPTIMIST.
explanation: An optimist expects the best; a pessimist expects the worst.

stem: Choose one word for: the killing of one's own father.
explanation: Patricide is killing one's father (pater). Matricide is killing one's mother, and homicide is killing any person.

stem: What does the idiom "to bury the hatchet" mean?
explanation: To bury the hatchet is to end a quarrel and become friends again.

stem: What is the cube root of 2744?
explanation: 14 × 14 × 14 = 196 × 14 = 2744. A cube ending in 4 has a cube root ending in 4.

stem: What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (8, 11)?
explanation: Distance = √[(8 - 2)² + (11 - 3)²] = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10. Adding 6 and 8 gives the wrong 14, and forgetting the square root gives 100.

stem: By selling an article for ₹450 a man loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 10%?
explanation: 450 is 90% of the cost, so cost = ₹500. A 10% gain means selling at ₹550. ₹495 wrongly adds 10% to the loss price.

stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 9 and their difference is 45. What is the smaller number?
explanation: The difference is 9 - 4 = 5 parts = 45, so one part is 9 and the smaller number is 4 × 9 = 36. 81 is the larger number.

stem: The Khilafat Movement in India was led by:
explanation: Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali led the Khilafat Movement, which Gandhi joined with the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920.

stem: Bihar's Muzaffarpur district is famous for which fruit?
explanation: Muzaffarpur is India's best-known litchi area, and its Shahi litchi has a GI tag.

stem: The French Civil Code of 1804 is better known as:
explanation: Napoleon's Civil Code of 1804 ended privileges based on birth and made all men equal before the law.

stem: Before its dams were built, the Damodar river was called the sorrow of:
explanation: The Damodar's floods once ravaged Bengal; the Damodar Valley Corporation (1948) built dams to control them.

stem: Which Harappan site is known for its dockyard?
explanation: Lothal, in Gujarat, had a brick dockyard linked to an old course of the Sabarmati, used for trade.

stem: What does inflation mean?
options: A rise in the number of banks
A fall in the value of exports
A general rise in prices over time
explanation: Inflation is a general rise in the price level, so each rupee buys less than before.

stem: Which Article of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India?
explanation: Article 63 creates the office of Vice-President. Article 52 creates the office of President, 72 is the pardoning power and 74 the Council of Ministers.

stem: The sex ratio is the number of females per how many males?
explanation: In India the sex ratio is stated as females per 1,000 males.

stem: Light travels at 2 × 10⁸ m/s in a medium. What is the refractive index of the medium? (Speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.)
explanation: Refractive index = speed in vacuum ÷ speed in the medium = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5.

stem: Washing soda is:
explanation: Washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. The others are baking soda, plaster of Paris and bleaching powder.

stem: Hydra reproduces asexually by:
explanation: A small bud grows on the side of a Hydra and separates into a new individual.

stem: Which blood group is called the universal recipient?
explanation: AB positive blood has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies and carries the Rh factor, so it can receive red cells of any ABO and Rh group. O negative is the universal donor.

stem: How many seats does the Bihar Legislative Assembly have?
explanation: The Bihar Vidhan Sabha has 243 elected seats (Karnataka has 224, Madhya Pradesh 230 and Gujarat 182). Bihar also has a Legislative Council, so its legislature is bicameral.

stem: National Science Day, marking the discovery of the Raman effect, is observed on:
explanation: C. V. Raman announced the Raman effect on 28 February 1928. 11 May is National Technology Day.

stem: Kanwar Lake (Kabartal), Bihar's first Ramsar site, is in which district?
explanation: Kanwar Lake in Begusarai is a large oxbow wetland left behind by a meandering river. It was designated in 2020 and is important for migratory birds.

stem: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat depicts:
explanation: The Statue of Unity, 182 m tall, near the Sardar Sarovar Dam, depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

stem: Mahatma Gandhi Setu across the Ganga links Patna with:
explanation: Mahatma Gandhi Setu, opened in 1982, joins Patna to Hajipur in Vaishali district.

stem: Which instrument measures wind speed?
explanation: An anemometer, usually spinning cups, measures wind speed. A barometer measures air pressure and an altimeter height.

stem: Which language of Bihar is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
explanation: Maithili was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003). Bhojpuri, Magahi and Angika are not in it.

stem: The national emblem of India is adapted from the Lion Capital found at:
explanation: The emblem comes from Ashoka's Lion Capital at Sarnath, with the motto Satyameva Jayate.
